This appeal is filed by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the award and decree dated 07.08.2018 passed in O.P.No.627 of 2011 by theChairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-SpecialSessions Judge for Trial of S.Cs/S.Ts (POA) cases-cum-Additional District Judge, at Nalgonda(for short "the Tribunal"), whereby the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- to the respondent No.1 herein-claimant for the injuries sustained by the respondent No.1 in a motor vehicle accident dated 24.06.2010.

sentences.text: Heard the submissions of learned counsel for both sides and perused the record.

3. The learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company contended that the Tribunal ought to have observed that the driver of the vehicle i.e, Tractor and Trailer bearing Nos.AP 24 R 5315 and 5316 did not hold a valid driving license on the date of the accident.

It is further contended that despite a notice issued under Ex.B1 to the owner of the vehicle (Respondent No.2 herein) to produce the license, no such document was furnished, leading to an adverse inference that the driver lacked the legal authority to drive.
Thus, it is argued that there was a clear violation of the terms of the insurance policy, and the Tribunal erred in fastening liability upon the Insurance Company.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.1- claimant contended that the Tribunal, after considering the oral and documentary evidence, rightly awarded the compensation and that no interference is required by this Court in the well-reasoned order passed by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: As seen from the material placed on record, the accident occurred on 24.06.2010 when the claimant was traveling on his motorcycle and was dashed by the offending Tractor and Trailer driven in a rash and negligent manner.
The police registered a case in Crime No.55 of 2010 for the offence under Section 338 of the IPC and subsequently filed a charge sheet (Ex.A2) against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Significantly, the Tribunal observed that the police investigation did not charge the driver for the offence of driving without a valid license under the Motor Vehicles Act.

In the absence of such a charge in the criminal proceedings, mere non-response of the owner to the Insurance Company's letter (Ex.B1) cannot be deemed sufficient proof of a fundamental breach of policy conditions.
6. Sofaras as quantum of compensation is concerned, the claimant sustained a fracture of the femur bone and underwent surgery with implants.

The Tribunal taking into account the medical bills (Ex.A4), nature of injuries and the subsequent pain and suffering, awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards special damages, including medical expenses and nourishment and Rs.50,000/- towards general damages (pain, suffering, and loss of future earnings), totaling Rs.1,00,000/-
.This Court finds no illegality or infirmity in the findings recorded by the Tribunal regarding the negligence of the driver of the crime vehicle or the quantum of compensation.
The grounds urged by the appellant do not warrant any interference with the well-reasoned impugned judgment.
This appeal is devoid of merits and the same is liable to be dismissed.
7. In the result, this appeal is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
